items.text: A group of citizens posted a video on social media showing that several trees in Shian Forest Park have been cut or burned. A member of this nature-loving group said that after following up with the responsible authority, the cause of this action was stated as "pest infestation."

The Judiciary Media Center reported the arrest of four citizens accused of promotional activities contrary to Sharia by making false and fabricated claims in religious and spiritual matters. Additionally, several other individuals related to this case have been summoned to the judicial authority.

Ali Parvin, former Persepolis coach, spoke about criticisms of Mehdi Tartaar during a farewell ceremony for Hassan Habibi at Amjadieh Stadium in Tehran. He said the team is at the top of the table and anyone can say anything. He added that the team can play poorly but if it gets three points, it matters, and asked if a team can play well and lose.

The US Treasury Department announced sanctions against several companies and individuals in India and Turkey for alleged cooperation with the Islamic Republic. These sanctions targeted a network in India accused of forging documents of ships carrying Iranian oil and a Turkish company for providing services to airlines sanctioned by the Islamic Republic.

Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that American voters' dissatisfaction was not only due to the war with Iran but also due to Trump's contradictory policies in this war. He emphasized that Democrats and Republicans do not differ in their goals regarding the Islamic Republic, and their main disagreement is over the method of confronting Tehran.
A video received by Iran International shows that two students trampled on a paper flag of the Islamic Republic during the mandatory rally on 13 Aban.

Bahman Abdi, Director General of the Planning and Social Participation Office of Youth at the Ministry of Sports and Youth, stated that registering 13-year-old girls on matchmaking platforms with family consent is not necessarily a legal violation under current laws. In response to the removal of the "Adam and Eve" matchmaking app from Google and Meta platforms, he said that registration of girls over 13 with family consent can be legally reviewed and cannot be simply considered a violation. Matchmaking centers have been advised to raise the minimum age for accepting girls to over 15 years.

Pouya Norouzi was wounded by direct gunfire from Khamenei's suppression forces on 20 Dey in Nourabad Mamasani and died in the operating room. His name remains in the memory of this land and his memory is a guiding light for freedom seekers.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of the national football team, said at the farewell ceremony for Hassan Habibi that working in the national team is difficult and referred to Ancelotti who did not achieve results with the Brazil national team despite his resume. He also stated that the national team has undergone a generational change and youth promotion, and they intend to increase the pace of this process.

The media office of Prince Reza Pahlavi, in response to the death sentence of Amirhossein Mousavi, a political prisoner, called for breaking the silence and raising the voices of political prisoners at risk of execution. On Thursday, 14 Aban, the office wrote on the social network X that Mousavi was arrested due to his activities on X and his death sentence was issued based on "forced confessions resulting from torture" in the "show trials of the Islamic Republic." Mousavi's lawyer announced on 13 Aban that his client was sentenced to death on charges of "corruption on earth" through activities on the social network X.

The Islamic Republic Broadcasting aired a live symbolic execution scene of Donald Trump, the US president, from Tajrish Square in Tehran. This public display was held after the Republicans' electoral defeat in the US midterm elections. In the scene, a person wearing a Trump mask and prisoner clothes played his role while spectators closely watched the performance.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump, despite delivering heavy military blows to Iran's regime structure, failed to turn these achievements into a political and lasting outcome and by declaring a ceasefire, gave the Islamic Republic a chance to rebuild. He added that after the US midterm elections, Trump faces three options: agreement with the Islamic Republic, resumption of military operations, or continuation of the current situation with sustained sanctions pressure.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Islamic Republic government is portraying the Republicans' defeat in the US midterm elections as if it had won the electoral campaign against Trump. He added that this triumphalist rhetoric does not reduce tensions with Washington and increases the risk of escalating tensions and military conflict. Kazemian also said that continuing the confrontation policy with the US will worsen the economic crisis and pressure on the lives of Iranian people.

Italian media reported the landing of an unidentified Italian jet at Mehrabad Airport and its eight-hour stop in Tehran. According to the newspaper Repubblica, the plane had turned off its transmitters at times during the flight from Rome to Tehran.

Mohammad Taghi Naqdali, a member of parliament, said there are "foot soldiers" in the streets of Europe and America willing to "bring American, Israeli, and European politicians to account," and the Islamic Republic is using these capacities. He stated that the response "without geographical limitation" can be carried out by missile or "visible and hidden hands" that are "close to the enemies." Naqdali said the economic interests and goals of America and Israel in the region are within the reach of the Islamic Republic, and Mojtaba Khamenei's order "has completely freed our hands to take practical action."
Aras Ahmadbeigi, an 18-year-old citizen from Ilam province, was released on Wednesday, 13 Aban, after posting bail.

As France prepared for nationwide strikes and protests on November 5, protesters in Paris set trash bins on fire and riot police were put on alert. French officials announced that about 70,000 police officers will be deployed across the country and between 500,000 to 700,000 people are expected to participate in protests outside Paris.

Gholamhossein Karbaschi, the editor-in-chief of Ham-Mihan newspaper, was sentenced by Branch One of the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province to one year in prison and two years of media activity ban. The prison sentence has been suspended for five years.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said in his first video message after the elections that radical Islam threatens the security and Jewish identity of Israel from two external and internal fronts. He described the Islamic Republic and its proxy groups as an external threat and parties supporting terrorism as an internal threat.

Financial Times reported that Russia has sold 90 advanced guided missile launchers to Iran to expand military cooperation with the Islamic Republic. According to the newspaper, the timing and details of the delivery of these equipment are not yet clear.

Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, said in his first video message after the elections that extremist Islam threatens the security and Jewish identity of Israel from two external and internal fronts. Netanyahu also accused opposition leaders of preventing the formation of a national government by setting impossible conditions.

Yesterday, following indiscriminate shooting by military forces in the Kheirabad area of Iranshahr county, one citizen died and another was injured. Additionally, a relative of the deceased citizen was arrested after inquiring about his condition and transferred to an unknown location.

Cristiano Ronaldo retired from Portugal's national football team on Thursday morning before the announcement of the new squad by Jorge Jesus. After 23 years in the national team, he ended his international career with 234 games and 146 goals. Ronaldo won three championships with Portugal and said farewell to the Portuguese people in a five-minute video.

Badr Al-Busaidi, Oman's Foreign Minister, and Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, in a phone call requested "practical arrangements" for maritime safety and joint technical mechanisms to ensure the unobstructed flow of trade and energy. The official Omani news agency reported on Thursday, 14 Aban, that the two ministers considered moving beyond de-escalation towards sustainable understandings necessary. The purpose of these arrangements is to "end the state of war and prevent the recurrence of conflicts" in the region.

The victory of the Democrats in the US midterm elections has elicited varied reactions among Iranian citizens. Some criticize Donald Trump's indecisiveness and delay regarding the Islamic Republic, while others believe the change in congressional majority will not prevent the US president from military action. Mehdi Tajik, a member of Iran International's editorial team, examines citizens' reactions to the election results and their assessment of Trump's future policy towards the Islamic Republic.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the prohibition of using children in military affairs, 600 female students from Hamadan and Kohgiluyeh and Boyer-Ahmad provinces were sent to "Rahian-e Noor" camps in the operational areas of southern Iran. Additionally, 5,300 other students from these two provinces will be sent to similar camps in later stages.

Several managers of private hospitals have reported the accumulation of claims from insurance companies, continuous increases in drug and equipment prices, and the growing difficulty in covering treatment costs. A hospital manager said that none of about 35 insurance companies and contracted institutions have settled their 1403 debts. Managers also reported a 600% increase in the price of Ringer's serum over three years and daily changes in drug prices.
Saeed Hasani, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Shiraz, was released from Adel Abad prison in Shiraz after posting a bail of six billion tomans. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Ali Falih al-Zaydi, the Prime Minister of Iraq, ordered the Military Industries Organization to coordinate with the Ministries of Defense and Interior, the Popular Mobilization Forces, and other security agencies to determine armament needs and supply them from domestic production. The Prime Minister's media office announced on Thursday, 14 Aban, that al-Zaydi, during a visit to this organization, called for the development of domestic production and private sector participation. He also ordered that contracts be signed directly with manufacturing companies and that intermediaries be removed to reduce corruption.

Mohsen Ardestani, head of the Geographical Organization of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic, said Israel knows it will one day be destroyed by the Islamic Republic and tries to delay this event through negative propaganda and war.

A video released on social media shows the parents of the late Mani Safarpour washing their son's motorcycle, which had been covered in dust for months. Mani Safarpour, 18, was targeted during the protests on 18 Dey 1404 in the Salsabil neighborhood of Tehran.

Six members of the medical staff at Fayyazbakhsh Hospital in Tehran were sentenced to one year of suspended imprisonment and six months of service in charitable institutions following labor protests. Additionally, several hospital employees faced cooperation termination, administrative violation cases, and salary benefit deductions.

Hossein Rasouli Nasab and Mehdi Zarif, two detainees from the nationwide protests of Dey 1404 in Shandiz who have been sentenced to death, remain imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Their death sentences have been confirmed by the Supreme Court and their cases have been sent to the execution unit. They were previously sentenced to death on charges including waging war through participation in destruction of public property and burning religious centers.

The Portuguese Football Federation reacted to Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from the national team by issuing a statement calling for a ceremony befitting his professional career. The federation appreciated Ronaldo's 234 national games and 146 goals and stated it will not allow his farewell to be held without proper respect. The statement said this will always be Ronaldo's home and thanked him for everything.

Aram News, citing Iraqi security sources, reported changes in the leadership structure of Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Kata'ib Hezbollah, and Harakat al-Nujaba. These groups are trying to transfer some of their political, economic, and security responsibilities to new figures.

The director general of forensic medicine in South Khorasan province announced that in the first half of the current year, 100 people died in traffic accidents in this province and 1410 were injured. Gholamabbas Azizi stated that among the deceased, 82 died in intercity accidents, 12 in urban accidents, and 6 on rural roads. September recorded 610 injuries, the highest number of traffic accident injuries among the months of the first half of the year.

Mohammad Hossein Sepehri, a protesting teacher, was released from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Wednesday, 13 Aban, after serving more than three years in prison. Sepehri was arrested by security forces in Mashhad in Mehr 1402 and transferred to Vakilabad Prison. He was sentenced by the court to a total of eight years in prison on various charges.

The Financial Times newspaper says it has obtained documents indicating that Russia has agreed to supply 90 guided missile launchers to the Islamic Republic of Iran. The newspaper stressed that the obtained documents do not specify whether the ordered launchers were ultimately delivered to Iran or not. The US State Department also announced it has sanctioned two individuals and one company for involvement in efforts to procure shoulder-launched anti-aircraft missiles for Iran.

A new wave of bomb threats on Thursday, 14 Aban caused disruptions in passenger flights in Europe and forced several planes to change course or make unscheduled landings. The Czech police announced that four planes heading to Prague faced bomb threats and police forces are preparing for their landings. Local Bulgarian media reported that three planes made emergency landings due to bomb threats.

Iran International identified a network of 690 individuals and 298 legal entities involved in the 88-day internet blackout in Iran in Dey 1404. Control of the internet in Iran is exercised through ownership of mobile operators Hamrah Aval, Irancell, and RighTel, and control of international internet gateways. Institutions affiliated with the Office of the Supreme Leader, the Revolutionary Guards, the Executive Headquarters of Imam, and the Mostazafan Foundation play a central role in this structure.

After the matchmaking app "Adam and Eve" was removed from Google Play and Meta platforms due to introducing 13-year-old girls as marriage options, the Director General of the Office of Youth Social Planning and Participation at the Ministry of Sports stated that according to the laws of the Islamic Republic of Iran, marriage of girls from age 13 with family consent is not illegal. He also recommended raising the minimum age for accepting girls in matchmaking centers to above 15 years.

Mohammad Jafar Qaempanah, the executive deputy of Masoud Pezeshkian, described the economic crisis in the country as an "economic war" and said that to win this war, there is no way but cooperation of the people and reduction of gas and electricity consumption. He emphasized the necessity of preventing gas cuts to industries and production disruption, and asked people to help manage energy shortages by lowering heating device temperatures and consuming less gas.
The Turkish Ministry of Defense announced that a soldier of this country was killed on Friday, 9 Aban, due to shooting from Iranian territory.

At least 14 European flights, including those of Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, Finnair, Ryanair, and LAT, on routes to Rome, Warsaw, Sofia, Brussels, Vienna, Bucharest, and Prague were targeted by bomb threats. Fighters from Italy, France, and Bulgaria escorted some planes, and several flights were diverted to alternate airports. The European Union stated it is still unclear whether these threats are connected and their origin and motive remain unknown.

Amir Delshad, detained during the January 1404 protests and held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, was sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court. An appeal request has been filed and the case referred to the Supreme Court. Charges include operational acts disrupting security and national interests and destruction of public property.

Harry Kane, captain of the England national team and winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or, has extended his contract with Bayern Munich until 2029. The 33-year-old striker, who joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023, has scored 156 goals in 161 matches for the club. Kane said he feels at home at Bayern Munich and is eager to win many more trophies with the club.
A new wave of bomb threats against passenger planes in Europe has led to flight route changes, emergency landings, and the deployment of military fighters to escort the planes.

A Finnair airplane took off from Rome's Fiumicino Airport after changing course due to a bomb threat. Italian Air Force fighters escorted the plane on its route from Helsinki to Rome. At least 14 European flights have been targeted by fake bomb threats on the third day of a week.

According to information received by Iran International, Mojtaba Saberi, a defrocked cleric and royalist prisoner, has been transferred to Behshahr prison due to holding a birthday party for Prince Reza Pahlavi in Sari prison. Saberi, sentenced to 38 months in prison, was arrested on 9 Dey 1404 after a speech at Farzad Khosh-Borash's 40th-day ceremony and spent several months in solitary confinement in Tirkelay prison in Sari. He has been subjected to pressure and torture during detention.

Jalal Ejadi, a sociologist, said that increasing purchasing power and wages, including a 10% increase in the minimum wage, are among the main demands of protesters in France. He added that labor unions and leftist forces support the protests and the government should negotiate with representatives of workers and students.

Today, Bijar farmers held a protest gathering against unpaid demands and the increase in prices of fertilizers, seeds, inputs, and agricultural tools. One of the farmers present warned that if the farmers' voices are not heard, these gatherings will continue.

Houman Shayani, a 33-year-old citizen from Nurabad Mamasani and a political activist detained in Dey month, released an audio message from prison about his and his family's situation and asked people for help to secure his release.

Some out-of-school children in interviews cited economic problems and their families' inability to afford education costs as reasons for dropping out. After leaving school, these children have turned to jobs such as street vending to help support their families. The interviews were conducted in the market area and workplaces of these children.

Three Ryanair planes flying from Madrid, Copenhagen, and London Stansted Airport to Bulgaria were targeted by bomb threats. Two planes landed in Sofia, but the flight from London was diverted to Plovdiv airport in the east of the capital. A spokesperson for the Bulgarian Ministry of Transport said more than 20 fake threats have been reported since the beginning of the week, with at least seven targeting Ryanair.

Rebar workers of the Zanjan National Housing Movement project have stopped working and gone on strike since Wednesday, 13 Aban. These workers say the current wages do not correspond to the difficulty of the work and living costs, and the increase in material prices and difficult working conditions have made continuing work at current rates economically unjustifiable for them.

Amnesty International stated that the Florida federal court ruling to continue legal proceedings against Parviz Sabeti, a former senior official of SAVAK, formalizes the right of torture victims under both the Shah's regime and the Islamic Republic. The organization considered this decision a step towards creating a legal basis for addressing repression and ending impunity.

Democrats defeated Republicans in the US midterm elections. The election result was partly influenced by voters' dissatisfaction with Donald Trump's performance. Mehdi Beigi examined the reasons for the Democrats' victory and the main factors of Americans' dissatisfaction with the Trump administration.

A report states that Jamileh (Mina) Mohammadamin-Azar and her husband Khoshnaw Azizpour, residents of Boukan, were arrested on Tuesday, 12 Aban [2026-11-03] by intelligence officers and taken to the security agency detention center in the county. Mr. Azizpour was released after several hours of interrogation, but the fate of his wife remains unknown.

Leili Golestan reported the cancellation of the cultural and literary event "Night Narrative" in Shiraz by order of the city authorities. The event was scheduled for Friday, 15 Aban, at Hafez Hall in Shiraz and had received a permit from the Ministry of Culture and Islamic Guidance. No specific reason has been given for the cancellation of the event.

Interfax news agency reported, quoting Dmitry Peskov, Kremlin spokesman, that Vladimir Putin met with Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, at the presidential palace. Iranian media had earlier reported that Putin and Rezaei spoke by phone on 11 Aban about the regional and global situation, focusing on West Asia. The Kremlin spokesman added that they emphasized the need to continue the strategic partnership between Russia and Iran based on an action plan developed by senior leaders of both countries.

Donald Trump told ABC News that he has received calls from people unhappy with Pete Hegseth, but he still "fully intends" to keep him as Secretary of War. Thomas Massie plans to bring an impeachment resolution against Hegseth to a vote next week, and several Republican sources expect the resolution to pass. Trump also confirmed that confirming the new Secretary of War will be easier before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Iran International viewers reported rising prices and shortages of bread, declining quality, and longer bakery queues. They also criticized the bread becoming smaller, changing color and taste, and going stale just minutes after purchase.

In the fifth week of the trial of three defendants accused of spying for the Islamic Republic against Iran International journalists, the judge in London on Thursday summarized the evidence and testimonies for the jury. The judge reviewed the testimony of Ali Ansari, an expert on Iranian affairs, recalling the history of actions by the Islamic Republic's security agencies against dissidents abroad and the role of the Ministry of Intelligence and the Revolutionary Guards in suppressing them.

Prince Reza Pahlavi, during his trip to Belgium, attended the Federal Parliament of Belgium after meeting with members of the European Parliament and holding a press conference there. The focus of his meetings in Brussels has been increasing pressure on the Islamic Republic and gaining practical support for the people of Iran.

Iranian media reported that Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, delivered a message from Mojtaba Khamenei, the leader of the Islamic Republic, to Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, during a meeting on Thursday at the Kremlin. Interfax news agency reported that Rezaei traveled to Moscow on an unannounced trip to meet and talk with Russian officials.

Manshe Amir, a Middle East expert, said that if Gadi Eisenkot is tasked with forming the Israeli government, Israel's entry into war with the Islamic Republic might be delayed. He pointed to the difference in approach between Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu towards the Islamic Republic.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, asked Yousef Jabareen, head of the Joint List, whether the list would leave the coalition if a large-scale military operation occurred in Iran or Gaza. Jabareen responded that they would make strategic decisions and that their people did not elect them to overthrow Netanyahu only to bring him back to power. Herzog said they are engaged in a fight against jihad, and Jabareen emphasized that there is no military solution and they will not cooperate with the far-right opposition under any circumstances.

Hundreds of Iranian migrants who served in the Revolutionary Guards have faced residency issues after the organization was designated as terrorist in Canada. Mahsa Mortazavi reports on a three-day gathering of affected families and their request to amend Canadian laws.

Mohammad Eslami, head of the Atomic Energy Organization, said Rafael Grossi, director general of the International Atomic Energy Agency, provides information to the enemies of the Islamic Republic. He also said Donald Trump's threats to attack Mount Koulak and other locations are a sign of American "desperation." Eslami added these actions misuse the powers of international bodies and reveal serious weaknesses in the UN Charter and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

On the evening of Wednesday, 13 Aban, following the announcement of the US election results, a show themed on the execution of Donald Trump, the US president, was held in Tajrish Square in Tehran and was broadcast live by the Islamic Republic's broadcasting organization. Earlier, a structure resembling a cell was installed in this square to depict Trump's imprisonment.

Ruhollah Rahimpour, a journalist and political analyst, said that Mohsen Rezaei personally going to Moscow to deliver Mojtaba Khamenei's message to Vladimir Putin is a clear sign of the decision-making constraints of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic and his strategic isolation.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, spoke by phone on Thursday, 14 Aban, with the foreign ministers of Turkey, Kuwait, Pakistan, Cyprus, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar about the latest regional developments. Iranian media reported that Araghchi discussed regional developments and diplomatic efforts and initiatives to maintain stability during these calls. In consultations with the Foreign Minister of Cyprus, the latest developments in bilateral relations and regional issues were also reviewed.

Debra Doring, a member of the German Federal Parliament and foreign policy spokesperson for the Green Party faction, accepted political sponsorship of Rashid Mazaheri, former goalkeeper of the Iranian national football team, and called for his immediate and unconditional release and an end to his solitary confinement. Doring stated that Mazaheri was arrested after openly criticizing the Islamic Republic and is currently in difficult conditions in prison. She warned about the possibility of a death sentence being issued and carried out for Mazaheri.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing visits to dozens of unknown graves in Fardis, Alborz province, and said: "We neither forgive nor forget."

Matlab Ahmadian, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, is facing deteriorating physical condition and cancer-related complications in his sixteenth year of imprisonment. Multiple surgeries and damage to his internal organs have made further surgery highly risky. The Tehran prosecutor opposes halting the sentence or granting him medical leave.

Interfax reported on Thursday, 14 Aban that the Russian Foreign Ministry, citing the ongoing risk of renewed tensions around Iran, advised its citizens to avoid traveling to Iran until conditions improve. Maria Zakharova, spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry, asked Russian citizens present in Iran to be vigilant and avoid gatherings, public events, and areas near military facilities and government buildings. She also urged Russian citizens to pay attention to official information released by Tehran and to follow the instructions of Iranian authorities.

On Thursday, 14 Aban, Bijar farmers protested over unpaid dues and rising prices of fertilizer, seeds, and agricultural inputs. Also, rebar workers of the National Housing Movement project in Zanjan have been on strike since Wednesday, 13 Aban, protesting that wages do not match living costs and the difficulty of work.

Media affiliated with the Islamic Republic claimed in a short video that Mohammad Karami, commander of the IRGC Ground Forces, visited Iranian islands in the Persian Gulf and the operational units under this force's control. In the video, Karami is seen wearing civilian clothes, riding a boat, and at times steering it.

The US State Department's Persian account announced on Thursday, 14 Aban, that Alireza Raeisi, 21, Alireza Sepahi, 24, and Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi were executed for participating in the protests of Dey 1404. The US State Department wrote that Raeisi and Sepahi were executed after secret trials and based on forced confessions. The US State Department stated that the Islamic Republic has responded to the peaceful demands of Iranian youth with violence, secret trials, and executions over 47 years.

Mehdi Tartaar, the head coach of Persepolis, reacted to accusations by Behnam Abolghasempour, CEO of Esteghlal Khuzestan, and emphasized that he will pursue the matter until the truth is clarified. Abolghasempour had claimed that Tartaar contacted a player from Esteghlal Khuzestan before a match and expressed interest in recruiting him. Tartaar denied these accusations and said that in 20 years of coaching and 18 to 19 years of playing, he has had no cases against him.

In Balochistan, fuel smuggling has become one of the few means of livelihood, but this dangerous activity is accompanied by shootings from military and law enforcement forces, sometimes without announcing a stop or prior warning. Reports indicate deaths and burnings of fuel smugglers on the roads, raising questions about adherence to legal regulations on the use of weapons in these areas. According to the law, shooting at vehicles is only permitted under specific conditions, but accounts suggest that officers sometimes act without following these rules.

The New York Times, citing five informed officials, reported that Iran and the US are considering "specific proposals" from mediators regarding the Islamic Republic's nuclear program. Qatar participated in two rounds of talks in Tehran last week and hosted a third round in Doha. The future of Iran's highly enriched uranium stocks is a major point of disagreement in the negotiations.

Videos received by Iran International show that the birthday ceremony of the immortal Behruz Nikkhah was held on Thursday, 14 Aban, at his gravesite. Behruz Nikkhah, 34 years old, was killed on 19 Dey 1404 in Fardis, Alborz province.

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, after meeting with Vladimir Putin, said Tehran has presented seven conditions to the United States and until they are implemented, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened and no negotiations will take place. Putin condemned US and Israeli attacks on Iran and expressed Russia's readiness to help end the war. The Rasht-Astara railway project was approved and the transfer of Russian gas to Iran was discussed.
A video received shows a group cutting trees with a chainsaw in Shian Park in Tehran. Shian is one of the largest and oldest forest parks in eastern Tehran.
Iran International reported that Trump is at a crossroads between continuing the siege or returning to war.

Some third-party employees of the National South Oilfields Company complain about the non-payment of their salaries for Mehr month by some contractors. They have requested the inspection units and complaint handling departments of the company to investigate the salary payment situation.

Mohsen Rezaee, head of the Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic, said on Thursday, 14 Aban, after meeting Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, that the two sides discussed regional developments and security arrangements after the war. Rezaee reported on the four-country meeting in Tehran, which Putin welcomed. He added that the Islamic Republic has announced seven conditions to the US, and until these are met, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened and no negotiations will take place.

A citizen reported to Iran International about extortion from the families of Fashafuyeh prison inmates with the promise of their children's release. According to this citizen, individuals use families' personal information to contact them and demand money in exchange for the prisoners' release. He added that despite paying money, his son was not released, and after following up, he realized that these calls were made by some prison staff.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the National Security Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, said that Democrats also dislike the Islamic Republic and Tehran must act carefully and with planning so that the US refrains from military actions in the region. He also predicted that in the near future, Congress and Donald Trump will clash and conflicts will arise between them.

Jalil Milanloui's daughter has released a video of her father's last meeting with her younger sister, Mahshid. She wrote in the video's description that Mahshid, a student in Tehran, saw her father for the last time in November of last year. According to her, Mahshid had her last phone call with her father on the evening of January 8, 2026, at 6 PM, and upon arriving in Esfarayen the next morning, she realized her father had been killed.
The head of the judiciary in Qom province reported obtaining the sixth victim family's consent in death penalty cases in the province this year.

Mohammad Javad Larijani, head of the Institute for Basic Sciences, described Mojtaba Khamenei as an "intellectual" and a "very capable jurist." Larijani said he has had many interactions with him and knows closely that he is very intelligent, precise, insightful, and patient. He also said that Mojtaba Khamenei grew up alongside his father and learned many lessons from his behavior, thoughts, and management style.

A video shows climbers installing a memorial plaque for Hamid Mahdavi on the Siah-Palas peak. Hamid Mahdavi, a 38-year-old firefighter, was killed by a direct bullet from officers on 18 Dey 1404 while helping the injured in Mashhad.

Barak Ravid, Axios reporter, quoted a US official saying the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier will make a multi-day stop in Singapore starting Friday and will not reach the US Central Command area of responsibility, CENTCOM, before mid-November (November 15, 2026). Fox News reported on October 20, 2026, that the Theodore Roosevelt strike group, along with the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit, has headed to the Middle East. Upon the arrival of this carrier, the number of US aircraft carriers in the region will reach three, and the number of additional forces in the area will reach about 10,000 sailors and Marines.

The sister of the disappeared Alireza Raeisi released a video showing that a tombstone was installed and a tree was planted for her brother's grave in the deserts around Anarak, Isfahan province. Alireza Raeisi, a 21-year-old protester and detainee from December 2025, was executed along with Alireza Sepahi at Dastgerd prison in Isfahan on the morning of Tuesday, 13 Mehr 1405 [Gregorian: 2026-10-05].

Jamshid Barzegar said the defeat of Republicans in the US Congress elections has increased pressure on Donald Trump and may push him toward an immediate agreement with the Islamic Republic or military action. He referred to increased diplomatic activities in Tehran, Mohsen Rezaei's trip to Moscow, and regional countries' mediation. Barzegar added that Trump has kept both options of negotiation and military attack open, and if diplomatic efforts do not quickly succeed, the likelihood of US military action will increase.

Jaber Rajabi, a political analyst, said that increased economic pressures and limited financial resources have reduced Tehran's ability to support proxy groups. He added that the Islamic Republic is trying to prevent further weakening of the proxy forces network by maintaining ties with groups close to it, especially the Houthis in Yemen. Rajabi predicted that if a new conflict begins, the participation of proxy groups will be more limited than before.

Citizens of some villages in the Jask district of Hormozgan province, including Heshdan, Kheirabad, Mohammadabad, Aliabad, and Sorgalam, have reported to Iran International through videos that their piped water has been cut off in recent months.

Mansheh Amir said Eisenkot needs the support of Arab parties to form the Israeli government, but the coalition parties' opposition to cooperating with them has made achieving the 61-seat majority difficult. Amir added that Netanyahu hopes Eisenkot will fail to form the cabinet so that he himself can get the chance to form the government. He also said Israel cannot start a new war against the Islamic Republic without the support of the US and currently assesses the likelihood of such an attack as low.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, announced that despite factions holding a total of 67 seats supporting Gadi Eisenkot to form a government, it is still unclear who has the ability to form the government. Herzog said factions with a total of 46 seats have proposed Benjamin Netanyahu, and mutual vetoes among and within blocs have complicated the situation. He said he will talk with some party leaders to clarify the situation and will assign the task of forming the government on Sunday.

A video received by Iran International shows the poor condition of the historic Pentecostal Church building in Kermanshah.
